messages:
Alice M.: Heads-up — the A/B rollout for routing-v2 is showing an unexpected lift in conversion. We pushed 60/40 but dashboard shows ~78/22. Can someone sanity-check sample ratio and instrumentation? cc @Ben (eng) @Carla - SRE

Ben (eng): Are you pulling that from experiments.redwood.com or the per-route console? Which metric exactly (conversion, error, latency)? :thinking:

Alice M.: Conversion = signup_success. Here's the dashboard snapshot: https://experiments.redwood.com/exp/9876 — look at variant counts and conv rate.

Carla - SRE: I noticed an infra change around 2026-03-15T12:33Z — a routing policy tweak landed that might affect sticky routing. Quick query I ran:
```sql
SELECT variant, count(*) as users, sum(signup_success) as conversions
FROM events
WHERE experiment_id=9876 AND ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15' AND '2026-03-15 13:00'
GROUP BY variant;
```
Results: variant A (control) users=12450 conversions=930; variant B (treatment) users=33780 conversions=26340.

David: Wait those counts are 27/73 split, not 60/40. That explains conversion skew. Why did B get so many users? :eyes:

Ben (eng): Hmm, could be sample routing using region-priority that recently got a precedence bump. We added a fallback route that sends traffic to v2 under capacity pressure — maybe that kicked in for a region with heavy weigh-in.

deploy-bot: [2026-03-15T12:32:54Z] deploy: routing-policy-service v1.14.0 deployed by @carla — change: bump region-priority for eu-west to prefer routing-v2.

Eva: If variant assignment depends on routing policy, our experiment validity is compromised. We should not make a business decision on this until we fix assignment determinism. Suggest pause ramp and rollback the routing tweak. :warning:

Carla - SRE: I can rollout a rollback to v1.13 within 5m. But note this will shift live traffic and may change user experience briefly.

Ben (eng): Agreed on pause. Also we should check if instrumentation deduped events or if SDK sends assignment post-facto for cached sessions. Quick sanity stats I did: control conv=930/12450=7.5% vs treatment conv=26340/33780=77.9%. p-value calculator (two-prop z): z~21, p~0.0 but sample is biased.

Alice M.: Right — statistically significant but not trustworthy. Action plan: 1) rollback routing-policy change (Carla) 2) pause experiment ramp in console (Ben) 3) run stratified audit by region & session-age (David) 4) re-run with forced deterministic assignment and re-check.

David: On audit, I'll run a join between assignment logs and routing decisions to see correlation:
```sql
SELECT r.region, a.variant, count(*) as users
FROM routing_decisions r
JOIN assignments a ON r.session_id = a.session_id
WHERE a.experiment_id = 9876 AND r.ts BETWEEN '2026-03-15' AND '2026-03-15 13:00'
GROUP BY r.region, a.variant;
```
If we see certain regions heavily favoring B that's the smoking gun.

Eva: Also recommend adding a guardrail: if observed sample ratio deviates >10% from expected for >5min, automatically pause ramp. We recently debated this but didn't implement. Can we add a short-term manual alert?

Ben (eng): I'll add a temp alert (ExpMonitor) to trigger on ratio drift and also flip experiment to hold at current traffic share.

Carla - SRE: Rollback started. I'll post when done.

deploy-bot: [2026-03-15T12:38:01Z] deploy: routing-policy-service rolled back to v1.13 by @Carla - SRE — status: success.

Alice M.: Thanks. Once rollback is verified, let's resume with deterministic assignment only and gate on the audit results. We'll also add the drift guard as a follow-up ticket.

Ben (eng): Filed FEAT-2142: "Experiment sample-ratio drift guard + alert" and set priority P1.

David: Audit queued, will post findings in ~30m. For now, holding decisions.

Eva: Good call. Note for postmortem: separate routing precedence changes from experiment rollout windows next time.

Alice M.: Agreed. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
